name: ext2_encode_extra_time
prose: Precondition: nsec is between 0 and 0x1FFFFFFF inclusive (so that nsec << 2 does not overflow int32_t; real nanosecond values up to 999999999 can exceed this bound and then rely on implementation-defined signed-shift behaviour), and sec is an int64_t for which sec - (int32_t)sec does not overflow int64_t (not every int64_t qualifies, e.g. values near INT64_MAX whose low 32 bits read as a negative int32_t). Postcondition: the function returns htole32(extra | (nsec << 2)) as a uint32_t, where extra = ((sec - (int32_t)sec) >> 32) & 3 (EXT3_EPOCH_BITS is 2 and EXT3_EPOCH_MASK is 3); that is, bits 0-1 of the value passed to htole32 are the epoch-extension bits of sec and bits 2-31 are nsec shifted left by 2. It reads only its arguments and has no side effects.
note: ext2_inode_cnv.c:240-248. Reviewer r1 (10-bit epoch) wrong: EXT3_EPOCH_BITS is 2 (ext2_dinode.h:83). Reviewer r2 (nsec<<2 overflows for nsec up to 2^30-1) right: int32_t shift, bound tightened to 0x1FFFFFFF. Reviewer r15 (sec - (int32_t)sec can overflow int64) right: precondition added. Contract left empty (htole32, endian).

name: ext2_rename
prose: The slice holds only the first lines of the function (its signature and declarations); this describes the whole static function ext2_rename (VOP_RENAME method, ext2_vnops.c:782-1149). Entry state assumed by the code: tdvp and, if non-NULL, tvp are locked and referenced; fdvp and fvp are referenced and not locked (the function itself calls vn_lock(fvp, LK_EXCLUSIVE) and later vrele(fdvp)). Exits: (1) label abortit, reached for a cross-mount rename (EXDEV), for tvp or tdvp flag violations (NOUNLINK/IMMUTABLE/APPEND on tvp or APPEND on tdvp, EPERM), for fvp == tvp (error is 0, nothing is renamed), for a vn_lock(fvp) failure, and, after unlocking fvp, for EMLINK (source link count at EXT4_LINK_MAX without EXT2F_ROCOMPAT_DIR_NLINK), EPERM (flags on the source or APPEND on its directory) and EINVAL (source directory is '.', is its own parent, has ISDOTDOT in either name, or already has IN_RENAME): it does vrele(tdvp) if tdvp == tvp else vput(tdvp), vput(tvp) if tvp is non-NULL, vrele(fdvp), vrele(fvp) and returns error. (2) Label bad then out, reached after the source link count has been bumped with ext2_inc_nlink and IN_CHANGE set: bad does vput of xp's vnode if xp is non-NULL and vput of dp's vnode; out clears IN_RENAME when a directory is being moved, re-locks fvp, and if that succeeds decrements the source link count, sets IN_CHANGE, clears IN_RENAME and vputs fvp, otherwise vrele(fvp); it returns error. Errors reaching bad: ext2_update failure on the source, the VOP_ACCESS result when a directory is moving to a new parent, ext2_inc_nlink(dp) or ext2_update failure on the new parent, ext2_direnter failure (the new-parent link count is undone first), EPERM for a sticky target directory, ENOTEMPTY for a non-empty target directory, ENOTDIR for a directory target with a non-directory source, EISDIR for a non-directory target with a directory source, and an ext2_dirrewrite failure. Errors going straight to out (tdvp is not vput by that path): ext2_checkpath and vfs_relookup failures in the directory-new-parent step. (3) Source-vanished exit: after the target has already been entered or rewritten, vfs_relookup of the source name is called; if it leaves fvp NULL the function does vrele(ap->a_fvp) and returns 0, without vput of fdvp and regardless of any relookup error value. (4) Normal exit: if the re-looked-up source is still the same inode, then for a directory with a new parent the old parent's link count is decremented and '..' is rewritten via vn_rdwr (errors of that read or write are ignored, a mangled '..' only logs ext2_dirbad); then ext2_dirremove(fdvp, fcnp) is called, on success the source link count is decremented, and IN_RENAME is cleared; if the re-looked-up name resolves to a different inode nothing is removed. It then does vput(fdvp) if dp is non-NULL, vput(fvp) if xp is non-NULL, vrele(ap->a_fvp) and returns the error left from vfs_relookup (when the inode matched, the ext2_dirremove result). An ext2_truncate failure on a replaced target directory is overwritten by the later relookup and is not returned. Directory entries already written are not rolled back after step 2, so on a late error the target entry may exist. The function panics if the directory/inode device vnodes differ, if the target and source inode numbers are equal, or if a replaced target directory has i_nlink > 2.
note: Slice ext2_vnops.c:517-795 ends right after the declarations (:782-794), so the body is not in the slice; fixed under real name. Reviewer o1 (state restoration not guaranteed) right: stated. Reviewer r15 (fvp/fdvp locked on entry and vput) wrong: code does vn_lock(fvp) at :831 and vrele(fdvp) at :862, so they are unlocked on entry. Own corrections vs old prose: vn_rdwr and ext2_truncate errors are not propagated (overwritten at :1035 and :1120); fvp == tvp returns 0 with no rename (:824-829).

name: ext2_rename
prose: Describes the whole static function ext2_rename (VOP_RENAME method, ext2_vnops.c:782-1149); the slice cut the tail. Entry state assumed by the code: tdvp and, if non-NULL, tvp are locked and referenced; fdvp and fvp are referenced and not locked (the function calls vn_lock(fvp, LK_EXCLUSIVE) itself and vrele(fdvp)). Exits: (1) label abortit, reached for a cross-mount rename (EXDEV), for tvp flag violations (NOUNLINK/IMMUTABLE/APPEND) or APPEND on tdvp (EPERM), for fvp == tvp (error is 0 and nothing is renamed), for a vn_lock(fvp) failure, and, after unlocking fvp, for EMLINK (source link count at EXT4_LINK_MAX without EXT2F_ROCOMPAT_DIR_NLINK), EPERM (flags on the source or APPEND on the source directory) and EINVAL (source directory is '.', is its own parent, ISDOTDOT in either name, or IN_RENAME already set): it releases tdvp (vrele if tdvp == tvp, else vput), vput(tvp) if non-NULL, vrele(fdvp), vrele(fvp) and returns error. (2) Labels bad and out, reached after the source link count was bumped (ext2_inc_nlink, IN_CHANGE): bad vputs xp's vnode if xp is non-NULL and dp's vnode; out clears IN_RENAME for a directory move, re-locks fvp and, if that succeeds, decrements the source link count, sets IN_CHANGE, clears IN_RENAME and vputs fvp, else vrele(fvp); returns error. Errors reaching bad: ext2_update on the source, the VOP_ACCESS result when a directory moves to a new parent, ext2_inc_nlink(dp) or ext2_update on the new parent, ext2_direnter, EPERM for a sticky target directory, ENOTEMPTY, ENOTDIR, EISDIR for target/source type mismatches, ext2_dirrewrite. ext2_checkpath and vfs_relookup failures in the new-parent step go to out directly, which does not release tdvp. (3) If, after the target was entered or rewritten, vfs_relookup of the source name leaves fvp NULL, the function does vrele(ap->a_fvp) and returns 0 regardless of any relookup error value and without vput(fdvp). (4) Normal exit: if the re-looked-up source is the same inode it, for a directory with a new parent, decrements the old parent's link count and rewrites '..' through vn_rdwr (read/write errors ignored), then calls ext2_dirremove(fdvp, fcnp), decrements the source link count if that succeeded and clears IN_RENAME; if the name now resolves to a different inode nothing is removed. It then vputs fdvp (if dp non-NULL) and fvp (if xp non-NULL), does vrele(ap->a_fvp) and returns the error left from vfs_relookup, or the ext2_dirremove result when the inode matched. The ext2_truncate result for a replaced target directory is overwritten and not returned; vn_rdwr errors are not returned. No rollback of directory entries already written occurs. It panics if the directory/inode device vnodes differ, if the target and source inode numbers are equal, or if a replaced directory target has i_nlink > 2.
note: Reviewer o1/r2 (source-vanished path returns 0 after target may be linked) right: stated (:1036-1049). Reviewer r15 (fvp == tvp returns 0 without renaming, prose says rename performed) right: stated (:824-829). Old prose wrongly listed vn_rdwr/ext2_truncate/VOP_ACCESS as always propagated; corrected (:1035, :1120, :896).

name: fuse_vnop_vptofh
prose: VOP_VPTOFH method for fusefs (slice cut the head; real name fuse_vnop_vptofh, defined at fuse_vnops.c:3317). Precondition: ap->a_vp is a vnode of a fusefs mount whose fuse_vnode_data and mount data are readable, and ap->a_fhp points to a buffer at least as large as struct fuse_fid. Return paths: (1) it returns EXTERROR(EOPNOTSUPP, ...) without touching the file handle if the session's dataflags lack FSESS_EXPORT_SUPPORT; (2) it returns EXTERROR(EOPNOTSUPP, ...) without touching the file handle if the mount has MNT_EXPORTED set and the server implements FUSE_OPENDIR (fsess_is_impl); (3) it returns the error from fuse_internal_getattr(vp, &va, curthread->td_ucred, curthread) if that is nonzero, without touching the file handle; (4) otherwise it sets fhp->len to sizeof(struct fuse_fid) and fhp->nid to the node's nid, and then, if the node's generation is at most UINT32_MAX, sets fhp->gen to it and returns 0, or, if the generation exceeds UINT32_MAX, returns EXTERROR(EOVERFLOW, ...) with len and nid already written and gen unwritten. No locks or references are acquired or released by this function itself; the fetched attributes in va are not used.
note: Slice cut the head; fixed under real name fuse_vnop_vptofh (:3317). Old prose said 'fuse_vptofh' and omitted that len/nid are written before the EOVERFLOW return (:3362-3367). No reviewer reason beyond the mechanical name mismatch.

name: msdosfs_setattr
prose: Precondition: ap->a_vp is a msdosfs vnode with a denode, and ap->a_vap and ap->a_cred are valid; fields the caller does not want to change hold VNOVAL, except va_type which must be VNON. Return paths in code order: (1) EINVAL if va_type != VNON or any of va_nlink, va_fsid, va_fileid, va_blocksize, va_rdev, va_bytes, va_gen != VNOVAL; (2) EINVAL if the vnode has VV_ROOT; (3) if va_flags != VNOVAL: EROFS on a read-only mount, then the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_ADMIN) error when cred->cr_uid != pm_uid and the check fails, then EOPNOTSUPP if va_flags has bits other than UF_ARCHIVE|UF_HIDDEN|UF_READONLY|UF_SYSTEM (all of these before any denode change), otherwise de_Attributes ARCHIVE/HIDDEN/SYSTEM bits (and READONLY for non-directories) are set or cleared from the flags and DE_MODIFIED is set; (4) if va_uid or va_gid != VNOVAL: EROFS on a read-only mount; VNOVAL values are replaced by pm_uid/pm_gid; if cred->cr_uid != pm_uid or uid != pm_uid or (gid != pm_gid and the caller is not a member of gid), the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_CHOWN) error is returned when that check fails; only after that, EINVAL if uid != pm_uid or gid != pm_gid (so EINVAL for a mismatching target is reached only by callers who pass the privilege check); (5) if va_size != VNOVAL: EISDIR for a directory, EROFS for a regular file on a read-only mount (other vnode types skip that check), then the vn_rlimit_trunc error, then the detrunc error; (6) if va_atime or va_mtime tv_sec != VNOVAL: EROFS on a read-only mount, the vn_utimes_perm error, otherwise the ADate (unless MSDOSFSMNT_NOWIN95 is set) and MDate/MTime are updated, ATTR_ARCHIVE is set for non-directories and DE_MODIFIED is set; (7) if va_mode != VNOVAL: EROFS on a read-only mount, the priv_check_cred(PRIV_VFS_ADMIN) error when cr_uid != pm_uid and the check fails, and for non-directories ATTR_READONLY is set or cleared from S_IWUSR, ATTR_ARCHIVE is set and DE_MODIFIED set (for a directory only the checks run); (8) finally it returns deupdat(dep, 0), which is 0 only if that call succeeds. Every early error return after step 3 can leave denode fields already modified by earlier steps (de_Attributes, de_flag with DE_MODIFIED, a truncated size, time fields); nothing is rolled back. The function acquires and releases no locks or references.
note: msdosfs_vnops.c:325-516. Reviewer o1 (later errors leave earlier modifications) right (:410, :463, :475-490). Reviewer r2 (va_type checked against VNON not VNOVAL) wrong against current prose, which already said VNON (:344). Reviewer r15 (priv_check_cred error comes before the EINVAL for uid/gid mismatch) right (:425-432): prose reordered.

name: nfsrv_acemasktoperm
prose: Static function at nfs_commonacl.c:265-353 (the slice also contains the unrelated nfsrv_buildace, nfs_aceperm and the start of nfsrv_buildposixace). Precondition: permp points to a writable acl_perm_t. The function converts an NFSv4 ACE access mask into FreeBSD ACL permission bits: it tests each of the 18 mask bits NFSV4ACE_READDATA, LISTDIRECTORY, WRITEDATA, ADDFILE, APPENDDATA, ADDSUBDIRECTORY, READNAMEDATTR, WRITENAMEDATTR, EXECUTE, SEARCH, DELETECHILD, READATTRIBUTES, WRITEATTRIBUTES, DELETE, READACL, WRITEACL, WRITEOWNER and SYNCHRONIZE, clears it from the local copy of mask, and ORs the corresponding ACL_* constant into a local perm (ACL_READ_DATA, ACL_LIST_DIRECTORY, ACL_WRITE_DATA, ACL_ADD_FILE, ACL_APPEND_DATA, ACL_ADD_SUBDIRECTORY, ACL_READ_NAMED_ATTRS, ACL_WRITE_NAMED_ATTRS, ACL_EXECUTE for both EXECUTE and SEARCH, ACL_DELETE_CHILD, ACL_READ_ATTRIBUTES, ACL_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES, ACL_DELETE, ACL_READ_ACL, ACL_WRITE_ACL, ACL_WRITE_OWNER, ACL_SYNCHRONIZE). Return paths: if any mask bit remains set after those 18 have been cleared, it returns NFSERR_ATTRNOTSUPP and leaves *permp unmodified; otherwise it stores the accumulated perm (the remapped ACL_* constants, not the mask value) in *permp and returns 0. The parameters acetype, owner and type are not used. It does not allocate or free memory and takes no locks.
note: nfs_commonacl.c:265-353. Reviewer r1, r2 (recognized bits wrong / stores perm not mask) right; r15 (stores remapped ACL_* constants, SEARCH maps to ACL_EXECUTE) right (:304-311, :348). Old prose stored mask & 0x1F01FF: wrong, rewritten. Contract left empty: acl_perm_t pointer and ACL_*/NFSV4ACE_* macro constants.

name: newnfs_connect
prose: Function newnfs_connect(nmp, nrp, cred, p, callback_retry_mult, dotls, clipp) at nfs_commonkrpc.c:252-542 (the slice cut the head; nmp == NULL means a userland upcall or NFSv4.0 callback, cred == NULL means a pNFS DS connect). Precondition: nrp is a valid nfssockreq whose nr_mtx is initialized and nr_nam holds a sockaddr, clipp points to the client slot (nrp->nr_client or an additional-connection slot), and either nrp->nr_cred or cred is a usable credential. The function replaces the current thread's td_ucred with nrp->nr_cred (or cred when nr_cred is NULL) and restores the original at the single exit label out, so both return paths restore it. It looks up a netconfig by address family and nr_sotype (getnetconfigent, result not checked for NULL), then creates a throw-away socket with socreate using that credential. Return paths: (1) if socreate fails it returns that error without closing anything and without touching *clipp; (2) otherwise it runs a soreserve loop that, on failure, decrements pktscale (never below 2) and retries; nr_sotype other than SOCK_DGRAM or SOCK_STREAM panics ('nfscon sotype'), but only if socreate already succeeded; the socket is closed with soclose after the loop, and if the last soreserve still failed that error is returned with *clipp untouched; (3) otherwise it creates a client with clnt_reconnect_create, applies CLNT_CONTROL settings that depend on nmp, cred and the mount flags (wait channel, interruptible, privileged port, TLS and cert name, soft-mount retries, NFSv4.1 DS timeout, backchannel creation under NFSD_LOCK with nfs_numnfscbd reference counting, retry count, UDP retry timeout), and then under nrp->nr_mtx, if *clipp is already non-NULL it releases the new client with CLNT_RELEASE and leaves the existing one, else it stores the new client in *clipp and, unless nmp is non-NULL with NFSMNT_NOCONN set, issues CLSET_CONNECT; it returns 0. No error return exists after the client is created.
note: Slice cut the head (function starts :252); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (invalid nr_sotype panic may be preceded by socreate failure) right (:320-323 precedes :354-355): qualified. Other prose claims checked against :281-541.

name: nfsv4_loadattr
prose: Function nfsv4_loadattr at nfs_commonsubs.c:1343-2610; the slice is a fragment from the middle of its attribute switch, so it is fixed under the enclosing function's real name. It parses an NFSv4 attribute bitmap and attribute-value list from the request/reply mbuf chain in nd, either storing the values or, when compare is nonzero, comparing them with local state. Precondition: nd holds a dissectable mbuf chain positioned at the attribute bitmap; retcmpp is non-NULL when compare is nonzero (it is dereferenced only in compare mode); vp is non-NULL for the compare cases that dereference it (e.g. FSID, CHANGEATTRTYPE). Flow: it calls nfsrv_getattrbits for the bitmap (in compare mode retnotsup is computed and copied into *retcmpp; otherwise default values are written into whichever of nap, sbp, fsp, pc, sfp and has_namedattrp are non-NULL), reads the value-list length, then loops over the bits in the bitmap, dissecting each attribute's XDR and adding its size to attrsum. In compare mode a mismatch sets *retcmpp to NFSERR_NOTSAME (or NFSERR_ATTRNOTSUPP in the ACL and unknown-attribute cases) only when *retcmpp is still 0, and the function itself still returns 0 for such mismatches; in non-compare mode values are stored through the corresponding out-pointers when they are non-NULL. An attribute bit the switch does not know prints a message, sets *retcmpp to NFSERR_ATTRNOTSUPP in compare mode if it was 0, and ends the loop without an error. Return value: 0 on success, or an error at one of these points: the error from nfsrv_getattrbits; NFSERR_BADXDR if attrsum exceeds the declared list length (checked at the top of each loop iteration and again after the loop), if a layout-type count is outside 0..32, or if an owner/group string length is out of range; EBADRPC (through NFSM_DISSECT) when the chain is too short; the errors of nfsrv_dissectacl, nfsm_getfh, nfsrv_getrefstr, nfsrv_mtostr and nfsm_advance for the attributes that use them; and the error of nfsm_advance when skipping trailing padding. All paths leave through the nfsmout label, which calls CURVNET_RESTORE; the function does not take ownership of the mbuf chain, and allocated temporary ACLs in compare mode are freed on the paths that follow their allocation (acl_free before goto nfsmout on error).
note: Slice 1604-1904 is the middle of nfsv4_loadattr (starts :1343), not a standalone item; fixed instead of dropped per HAND_METHOD rule 6 (real function exists, head cut). Header comment of the function ('retcmpp is 1 if all same') is stale: code sets 0/NFSERR_NOTSAME/NFSERR_ATTRNOTSUPP (:1385, :2584). Detail on individual attributes in the sections after :1474 not enumerated.

name: nfsv4_fillattr
prose: Function nfsv4_fillattr at nfs_commonsubs.c:2832-3555 (the packet slice 1905-2205 actually lies inside nfsv4_loadattr, so the earlier prose described a different function and the reviewer's compare-mode remark concerns that slice, not this function). It encodes the attributes selected by *attrbitp into nd and returns the number of bytes appended. Behaviour depends on the caller kind: with p == NULL and cred == NULL (client-side setattr) it clears non-settable bits and uses saclp as the single ACL of the type whose bit is set; otherwise (server reply or callback) it clears non-fillable bits and allocates three temporary ACL buffers (naclp, npaclp, ndaclp). It then calls nfsvno_getfs, allocates a statfs buffer, and if any statfs-based bit is set calls VFS_STATFS(mp). Return paths: (1) normal path: it appends the bitmap (nfsrv_putattrbit), a count word, and the encoded value of every bit still set, frees all three ACL buffers (those that were allocated) and the statfs buffer, stores the value-byte count into the count word, and returns the number of bytes appended including the bitmap and count word; (2) three early returns of 0 that append nothing: VFS_STATFS failure when reterr is nonzero (nd_repstat = NFSERR_ACCES), failure of the NFSv4 ACL fetch (NFSVOPLOCK failing gives NFSERR_PERM, otherwise VOP_ACCESSX or VOP_GETACL error) when reterr is nonzero (nd_repstat = NFSERR_ACCES), and failure of the POSIX access-ACL fetch when reterr is nonzero (nd_repstat = NFSERR_INVAL). These early returns free the statfs buffer but not the naclp/npaclp/ndaclp buffers that were allocated on the server/callback path. When reterr is zero those fetch failures merely clear the corresponding bit (NFSv4 ACL, POSIX access ACL, STATFS bits); a POSIX default-ACL fetch failure never returns an error and just sets ndaclp->acl_cnt to 0. The function takes the vnode lock (LK_SHARED) only temporarily around ACL fetches. An unknown bit in the loop prints a message and appends nothing.
note: Slice 1905-2205 is inside nfsv4_loadattr (:1343-2610), not nfsv4_fillattr (:2832); fixed under the packet's name with prose for the real nfsv4_fillattr. Old prose claimed the statfs buffer is freed on every return (true) and ACL buffers freed on normal path (true) but omitted that the three early returns leak the ACL buffers (:2897-2899, :2938-2942, :2963-2967). Reviewer r15 (omits compare mode) concerns the loadattr slice: not applicable to nfsv4_fillattr.

name: nfsm_advance
prose: Function nfsm_advance(nd, offs, left) at nfs_commonsubs.c:835-877 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). Precondition: nd points to a descriptor whose nd_md is a valid mbuf and nd_dpos points within it, and left is either -1 (the function then computes the bytes remaining in nd_md past nd_dpos as m_len minus the offset of nd_dpos) or the caller's own count of those remaining bytes (which the function does not verify). Return paths, all through label out: (1) offs == 0: returns 0 and changes nothing; (2) offs < 0: prints a diagnostic and returns EBADRPC with the position unchanged; (3) offs > 0: while offs exceeds the bytes left in the current mbuf it subtracts them, moves nd_md to the next mbuf, and sets nd_dpos to the start of that mbuf's data; if the next mbuf pointer is NULL it returns EBADRPC with nd_md set to NULL and nd_dpos left at the start of the last mbuf it successfully entered, or at its original value if the very first step already fell off the chain; (4) otherwise it adds the remaining offs to nd_dpos and returns 0. When offs equals the bytes left in the current mbuf the position ends at the end of that mbuf and nd_md is not advanced. The caller keeps ownership of the chain; no locks or references are taken.
note: nfs_commonsubs.c:835-877. Reviewer r1 (nd_md set to NULL on exhaustion) right (:864-868). Reviewer r2 (nd_dpos remains at prior position) right only when the first step fails; after crossing at least one mbuf nd_dpos is the start of the last reached mbuf (:870): old prose already said this. Added the offs == left boundary.

name: nfscl_nget
prose: Function nfscl_nget(mntp, dvp, nfhp, cnp, td, npp, lkflags) at nfs_clport.c:117-305 (the slice ends mid-function). Precondition: mntp is an NFS mount, dvp is a directory vnode on it whose nfsnode has a non-NULL n_fhp, nfhp is an M_NFSFH-allocated struct nfsfh with nfh_len bytes in nfh_fh that the function takes over, cnp is a valid componentname, npp is writable. *npp is set to NULL first. If the mount has NFSMNTP_FAKEROOTFH and nfhp equals the mount's file handle, nfhp is freed and replaced by a freshly allocated fake-root handle. Return paths: (1) vfs_hash_get fails: nfhp is freed and the error returned with *npp NULL; (2) vfs_hash_get finds a vnode that is then seen as VN_IS_DOOMED: the function calls only vrele on it (it does not release any lock vfs_hash_get took according to lkflags), frees nfhp and returns ENOENT with *npp NULL; (3) vfs_hash_get finds a live vnode: for an NFSv4 regular file whose stored parent handle or name differs it replaces n_v4 under the nfsnode mutex, frees the old and any unused new node, sets *npp to its nfsnode, frees nfhp and returns 0, the vnode being referenced and locked as vfs_hash_get returned it for lkflags; (4) no vnode found: a new nfsnode and vnode are allocated; if getnewvnode fails, the nfsnode and nfhp are freed and the error returned (*npp NULL); the new vnode is given nfhp as n_fhp, NFSv4.0 mounts attach a copy of the parent handle and name, and it is locked exclusively with lockmgr; if insmntque fails the nfsnode pieces, nfhp and n_v4 are freed and the error is returned with *npp NULL; (5) vfs_hash_insert is then called with lkflags: if it returns an error that error is returned with *npp NULL (nfhp is not freed here; it was attached as np->n_fhp and is left to vnode teardown); if it returns an existing vnode (another thread won the race) *npp is set to that vnode's nfsnode and 0 is returned (the losing vnode is released inside vfs_hash_insert); otherwise *npp is the new nfsnode and 0 is returned. On every nonzero return *npp is NULL, but after path (2) a vnode lock obtained by vfs_hash_get may remain held.
note: nfs_clport.c:117-305. Reviewer r15 (ENOENT path calls only vrele while vfs_hash_get returned nvp locked, so 'no lock left' is false) right (:161-166): prose changed. Also corrected: on the vfs_hash_insert error path nfhp is not freed here (:293-296), and in the existing-vnode path nfhp is freed, never attached (:217).

name: nfscl_loadattrcache
prose: Function nfscl_loadattrcache(vpp, nap, nvaper, writeattr, dontshrink) at nfs_clport.c:438-607 (slice cut the tail). Precondition: *vpp is an NFS vnode with nfsnode VTONFS(vp), nap points to a filled-in nfsvattr, nvaper is NULL or points to a struct vattr, and the caller keeps its own vnode references and locks. The function locks the nfsnode mutex at the start (NFSLOCKNODE) and does not unlock it itself; the unlock is done by ncl_pager_setsize(vp, NULL), which the code at label out always calls before returning (that helper's comment says the node is unlocked unconditionally when its second argument is NULL). It returns 0 or EIDRM, both via label out. Steps: if vp->v_type differs from nap's va_type it sets v_type (and v_op to newnfs_fifoops for VFIFO) and np->n_mtime. If writeattr is nonzero it copies only na_filerev, na_size, na_mtime, na_ctime, na_btime, na_fsid and na_mode from nap into the node's cached attributes and performs no fileid check. If writeattr is zero and either the nfscl_force_fileid_warning fail point fires or the cached fileid is nonzero, differs from nap->na_fileid, and is not the combination (cached fileid 2, syskrb5 mount option set, node file-handle length NFSX_FHMAX+1), it calls nfscl_warn_fileid, leaves the cached attributes unchanged and returns EIDRM (skipping all later steps, so nvaper is not filled; v_type and n_mtime may already have been changed); otherwise it copies the whole nfsvattr into the node's cache. On every non-EIDRM path it then recomputes va_fsid (vn_fsid, with a 64-bit hash of na_filesid for NFSv4 mounts whose root fsid differs), sets n_attrstamp to the current time, reconciles the cached size with n_size (for regular files, with dontshrink it keeps the larger size and zeroes n_attrstamp; with NMODIFIED set it keeps the larger of the two sizes; otherwise it adopts the server size and sets NSIZECHANGED), zeroes n_attrstamp if the cached mtime moved backwards, and, whenever nvaper is non-NULL, copies the cached attributes into *nvaper (via ncl_copy_vattr) and overrides atime/mtime with the pending local values when NCHG together with NACC/NUPD is set.
note: nfs_clport.c:438-607. Reviewer o1 (fileid mismatch does not always give EIDRM: fileid 0 and syskrb5 fileid 2 exceptions) already handled in prose (:504-508). Reviewer r2 (nvaper copied whenever non-NULL, also with writeattr) right and already in prose (:590-598). Refined: nfsnode mutex is released by ncl_pager_setsize (:605), not by this function directly; EIDRM path does not fill *nvaper.

name: nfsrpc_readdir
prose: The slice is the middle of nfsrpc_readdir(vp, uiop, cookiep, cred, p, nap, attrflagp, eofp) at nfs_clrpcops.c:3467-3935 (there is no function named nfscl_readdir), so it is fixed under its real name. Precondition: vp is an NFS directory vnode; uiop has exactly one iovec in kernel space (UIO_SYSSPACE) and uio_resid is a multiple of DIRBLKSIZ (both KASSERTed); cookiep holds the resume cookie (zero for the first call). The function never takes the nfsnode lock except briefly around the cookie verifier (n_cookieverf) accesses. It sets *attrflagp to 0 (and again before each RPC), and *eofp to 0 if eofp is non-NULL. For NFSv4, when uio_offset == 0, it first sends a LOOKUPP/GETFH/GETATTR compound and builds synthetic '.' and '..' dirent records (cookie 0) into the buffer. It then loops sending READDIR RPCs of at most the mount's readdir size (reduced to uio_resid plus one DIRBLKSIZ when larger), converting each reply entry into a dirent followed by an 8-byte cookie, skipping entries whose name nfscl_invalidfname rejects, updating *cookiep after each stored entry, until the server reports no more entries or the next entry would not fit (bigenough becomes 0). It pads the last block to DIRBLKSIZ, then sets *eofp (if non-NULL) to 1 if no bytes were consumed, to 0 if it stopped because the buffer was full, else to the server's eof flag, and appends empty DIRBLKSIZ records while uio_resid is nonzero and differs from its starting value. Return paths: (1) nfscl_request error: returned directly (also for the initial LOOKUPP request); (2) NFSv4 initial lookup: an nfsm_loadattr/NFSM_DISSECT failure goes to nfsmout; a nonzero nd_repstat other than NFSERR_NOENT, or an error from nfsm_advance, EPERM for a file handle length outside 1..NFSX_V4FHMAX, or an error from nfsv4_loadattr, is returned after freeing the reply (NFSERR_NOENT is treated as the root: '..' reuses the '.' fileid and processing continues); (3) in the loop, a nonzero nd_repstat is returned as the error, EBADRPC is returned for a name length <= 0 or > NFS_MAXNAMLEN, and errors from NFSM_DISSECT, nfsm_mbufuio, nfsm_advance, nfsv4_loadattr, nfscl_postop_attr go to nfsmout; (4) normal completion falls into nfsmout with error 0. nfsmout frees the reply mbuf chain if nd_mrep is still non-NULL and returns error; on the error paths that go through it, eofp is not updated by the normal-completion code, entries already stored remain in the buffer, uio_resid/uio_offset/iov may already be advanced past a partly built entry, and *cookiep may already hold the cookie of the last entry fully stored.
note: Slice cut head; real function nfsrpc_readdir (:3467). Old prose wrong on: 'dnp node lock released' (function holds no node lock across the call), 'EBADRPC for an invalid file name' (invalid names are skipped, EBADRPC only for length out of range :3730), uio_offset multiple of DIRBLKSIZ (not asserted), and cookie left unchanged for failed entry (cookie updated after each stored entry :3859-3862). Dropped-status record reversed to fix because the function exists.

name: nfs_mount
prose: Static function nfs_mount(mp) at nfs_clvfsops.c:903-1490 (the slice starts in the middle of its option parsing). Precondition: mp is an NFS mount being created or updated and mp->mnt_optnew holds the nmount options, which may include either a binary 'nfs_args' option or new-style string options. The function allocates two MNAMELEN buffers (hst, dirpath) and parses options into a struct nfs_args; all exits go through label out, where, if error is 0, it sets MNTK_LOOKUP_SHARED, MNTK_NO_IOPF, MNTK_USES_BCACHE (and MNTK_NULL_NOCACHE for NFSv4 mounts) in mnt_kern_flag under the mount interlock, and in every case frees nam, tlscertname, hst and dirpath (nam and tlscertname are set to NULL after the mountnfs call because that function takes them over). Return values: EINVAL if vfs_filteropt rejects an unknown option, if tlscertname is NULL, 1 char or longer than NAME_MAX - 6 bytes, if readdirsize, readahead, wsize, rsize, retrans or timeo/timeout is not a positive integer, if actimeo, acregmin/max, acdirmin/max, wcommitsize, nametimeo or negnametimeo is not a valid non-negative integer, if minorversion is outside 0..2 or NFSv4 is not selected, if nconnect is outside 1..NFS_MAXNCONN, if nconnect is used with something other than NFSv4.1/4.2 over TCP, if syskrb5 is used without NFSv4.1/4.2, without sec=krb5[ip], or together with gssname, if the file handle size is out of range, if no hostname is given, if the hostname is MNAMELEN bytes or longer, or if no server address option is present; EPROGMISMATCH if the nfs_args version differs from NFS_ARGSVERSION; EIO if MNT_UPDATE is set and the mount has no nfsmount; ENAMETOOLONG if the 'addr' option is larger than SOCK_MAXADDRLEN or if copyinstr rejects an over-long hostname from a user nfs_args; the error from vfs_copyopt, copyin, copyinstr, getsockaddr or nfs_mountroot; the error from mountnfs; and 0 otherwise. When MNT_ROOTFS is set (without MNT_UPDATE) and nfs_diskless_valid is nonzero, the result of nfs_mountroot is returned and no options are parsed. When MNT_UPDATE is set (and an nfsmount exists) the version, security, lockd and oneopenown flags are kept from the existing mount, nfs_decode_args is called and the function leaves through out with error 0 (a TCP-to-UDP change only logs a warning).
note: Slice cut the head (function starts :903); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (over-long copyinstr hostname gives ENAMETOOLONG not EINVAL) right: copyinstr result is returned as is (:1325-1327); the new-style over-long hostname still gives EINVAL (:1366-1369). Old prose lacked ENAMETOOLONG for 'addr', the syskrb5/nconnect conflicts, and the out-label side effects.

name: nfsvno_open
prose: Function nfsvno_open(nd, ndp, clientid, stateidp, stp, exclusive_flagp, nvap, cverf, create, aclp, daclp, attrbitp, cred, done_namei, exp, vpp) at nfs_nfsdport.c:1969-2124 (the slice also contains the tail of nfsvno_fsync and nfsvno_statfs). It returns void; results are in nd->nd_repstat and *vpp. Precondition: ndp holds the results of nfsvno_namei (ni_vp is NULL for a new file, otherwise a locked referenced vnode; ni_dvp is locked and referenced when create is NFSV4OPEN_CREATE or the file is new), nd->nd_repstat is the status so far, and vpp is writable. Behaviour by case: (1) If ni_vp is NULL, nfsrv_opencheck is called first and its status replaces nd_repstat; if it turns a zero status nonzero, done_namei is set to true. (2) If nd_repstat is 0 and ni_vp is NULL (new file): nvap's na_flags are set to VNOVAL around VOP_CREATE and restored; on VOP_CREATE success nfsrv_pnfscreate is called; ni_dvp is released through VOP_VPUT_PAIR and the path buffer is freed (nfsvno_relpathbuf) whether or not the create succeeded. On success, with *exclusive_flagp not NFSV4_EXCLUSIVE_NONE, it sets the verifier into the atime via VOP_SETATTR: if that fails the new vnode is vput, ni_vp becomes NULL and nd_repstat is set to NFSERR_NOTSUPP; if it succeeds it calls nfsrv_fixattr for NFSV4_EXCLUSIVE_41 when owner, group, time-modify-set, archive, hidden, system or an ACL was supplied, and sets NFSATTRBIT_TIMEACCESS in the attribute bitmap; in either exclusive case *exclusive_flagp is then set to NFSV4_EXCLUSIVE_NONE. Without exclusive create it calls nfsrv_fixattr (non-exclusive mode). vp is then ni_vp, which is NULL when creation or the exclusive SETATTR failed. (3) If nd_repstat is 0 and ni_vp exists: the path buffer is freed; vp is ni_vp; if create is NFSV4OPEN_CREATE, ni_dvp is released (vrele if it is the same vnode as vp, else vput); if a size is set and the vnode is regular it calls nfsvno_accchk(VWRITE), then nfsrv_opencheck and, if both pass, nfsvno_setattr with only the size; otherwise for a regular file it calls nfsrv_opencheck. Here vp stays the existing vnode (referenced and locked, non-NULL) even if a check set nd_repstat nonzero; non-regular files get no further check. (4) If nd_repstat was nonzero (on entry, or from the step-1 opencheck) and done_namei is true: it asserts create == NFSV4OPEN_CREATE, frees the path buffer, releases ni_dvp (vrele if equal to ni_vp, else vput) and vputs ni_vp if non-NULL, and vp stays NULL. (5) If nd_repstat was nonzero and done_namei is false, nothing is released. In all cases *vpp = vp is stored last.
note: nfs_nfsdport.c:1969-2124. Reviewer o1 (existing ni_vp on failure gives non-NULL *vpp) right (:2074, :2121). Reviewer r2 (done_namei cleanup vputs the vnode and gives NULL *vpp) right (:2104-2120): both described as separate cases. Reviewer r15 (size-set existing-file path uses nfsvno_setattr not nfsrv_fixattr; *vpp stays non-NULL after failed check) right (:2096): old prose corrected. Old prose also said ni_dvp is released on existing-file path only when create == NFSV4OPEN_CREATE (right) and exclusive-flag always reset when exclusive branch taken (right).

name: nfsvno_fsync
prose: There is no function nfsvno_commit; the slice contains the body of nfsvno_fsync(vp, off, cnt, cred, td) (nfs_nfsdport.c:1826-1919), which implements the COMMIT flush, so it is fixed under that name. Precondition: vp is a vnode on a mounted filesystem, whose f_iosize is a power of two when the buffer-cache branch is taken; cred is not used. Behaviour: if cnt == 0, cnt > MAX_COMMIT_COUNT, or the mount does not have MNTK_USES_BCACHE set, it calls vnode_pager_clean_sync(vp) and returns the result of VOP_FSYNC(vp, MNT_WAIT, td). Otherwise it widens [off, off+cnt) to iosize and page boundaries, cleans the vnode's VM object synchronously over that range if it might be dirty (vm_object_page_clean with OBJPC_SYNC), then walks the logical blocks of the range under the buffer-object lock: for each buffer found by gbincore it locks it (retrying on ENOLCK), and if it has B_DELWRI and not B_INVAL it clears B_ASYNC and writes it synchronously with bwrite (counting nfs_commit_miss), otherwise unlocks it; nfs_commit_blks is incremented per block. In this second branch the function returns 0 regardless of bwrite or page-clean outcomes, since error is never assigned there. So the return value is the VOP_FSYNC error only in the whole-file branch.
note: Dropped item named nfsvno_commit does not exist in the tree; the real function in the slice is nfsvno_fsync (:1826), so it is fixed rather than dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said all B_DELWRI buffers are written and result is an NFS error code: wrong (only buffers found in range, errors of bwrite not returned).

name: nfsrvd_getattr
prose: Function nfsrvd_getattr(nd, isdgram, vp, exp) at nfs_nfsdserv.c:238-396 (the slice starts after its head and also contains the beginning of nfsrvd_setattr). Precondition: if nd->nd_repstat is 0 on entry, vp is a locked, referenced vnode that this function takes over. If nd->nd_repstat is nonzero on entry it jumps straight to the exit and returns 0 without touching vp (the caller keeps its lock and reference). Return value: 0, except (a) for NFSv4, the error returned by nfsrv_getattrbits when the attribute bitmap cannot be parsed, with vp released by vput, and (b) NFSERR_INVAL when the bitmap contains time_access_set or time_modify_set, with vp released by vput. All other failures are reported only in nd->nd_repstat, with the function returning 0. NFSv4 flow: if nfsv4root_getreferral finds a referral for vp, nfsrv_putreferralattr builds the referral attributes (it may set nd_repstat itself, e.g. to a moved-type status), vp is vput and the function returns 0; otherwise nfsvno_accchk is run for VREAD_ACL/VREAD_ATTRIBUTES when needed. Then nfsvno_getattr is called (when nd_repstat is still 0); for NFSv4 nfsvno_getfh (if the file handle is requested) and nfsrv_checkgetattr follow; on any of these failing, vp is vput. On NFSv4 success it gathers pathconf/extended attribute facts, optionally takes a reference on the covered vnode of a root directory (VREF/NFSVOPLOCK/VOP_GETATTR then vput or vrele of that vnode, its error going to nd_repstat), takes vfs_ref and vfs_busy on the mount (vfs_busy's error goes to nd_repstat, vfs_rel is always called, vfs_unbusy only if busy succeeded), unlocks vp with NFSVOPUNLOCK, calls nfsvno_fillattr when nd_repstat is 0, and finally releases vp with vrele (not vput, since it was unlocked). For NFSv2/v3 it fills the reply with nfsrv_fillattr and vput(vp). When nfsvno_getattr fails for any version, vp is vput. In every path in which the function took over vp, vp is released exactly once and no temporary vnode or mount reference acquired here remains.
note: nfs_nfsdserv.c:238-396. Reviewer r15 (omits nfsrv_putreferralattr setting nd_repstat on referral path) right (:272-273): added. Rest of old prose checked against :258-391 and kept.

name: nfsrvd_open
prose: The slice is the middle of the NFSv4 OPEN service nfsrvd_open(nd, isdgram, dp, vpp, fhp, exp) at nfs_nfsdserv.c:3054-3622 (there is no function nfsrv_open in this file), so it is fixed under its real name. Precondition: nd holds a request positioned at the OPEN arguments, dp is the directory (or, for the FH-style claims, the file) vnode which this function takes over, and vpp is writable. It allocates the nfsstate (stp, with the owner string), and two temporary ACL buffers (when NFS4_ACL_EXTATTR_NAME is defined); none of these are caller-provided. Almost every protocol error is reported in nd->nd_repstat while the function itself returns 0: the function returns a nonzero value only when NFSM_DISSECT fails (EBADRPC), or nfsrv_mtostr, nfsv4_sattr or nfsrv_parsename return an error. Return paths: (1) label nfsmout (reached for a malformed or short request, owner length not in 1..NFSV4_OPAQUELIMIT, unknown create 'how' or create value, unknown claim or claim-previous delegation type, a pending nd_repstat before the name lookup, and the nfsv4_sattr/mtostr errors): vrele(dp), frees the ACLs and stp, and returns error (0 when only nd_repstat, such as NFSERR_BADXDR, was set); (2) nfsrv_parsename failure: vrele(dp), frees the ACLs, stp and the path buffer, returns that error; (3) normal end: it returns 0. On that path the access/delegation checks and nfsrv_openctrl run only while nd_repstat is 0, vp is unlocked, stp is freed if still non-NULL, the parent's post-op attributes are fetched when nd_repstat is 0, and if nd_repstat is still 0 the reply (stateid, change info, rflags, attribute bitmap, delegation information) is marshalled and *vpp = vp (the caller then owns that reference), otherwise a non-NULL vp gets vrele; dirp is vrele'd if non-NULL and both ACL buffers are freed. nd_repstat values set in this code include NFSERR_INVAL (bad access or deny value, create with a claim other than null, exclusive create in a named-attribute directory, time_access_set with exclusive-41, create with the FH-style claims), NFSERR_BADXDR, EEXIST (guarded create of an existing file, or exclusive-create verifier mismatch), NFSERR_PERM (doomed vnode in the FH claims), NFSERR_ISDIR or NFSERR_SYMLINK for a non-regular file, and statuses from nfsrv_opencheck, nfsvno_namei, nfsvno_open, nfsvno_accchk, nfsvno_getattr and nfsrv_openctrl.
note: Slice is inside nfsrvd_open (:3054); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (lock-state storage is allocated and freed here, not caller-provided) right (:3099, :3471). Old prose also wrongly said the function returns a nonzero status stored in nd_repstat for protocol errors: it returns 0 for those (nd_repstat only, :3096-3097, :3246-3250) and said 'in every path' it releases everything, which only holds with the per-path qualifications above.

name: nfsrvd_deallocate
prose: The slice covers the tail of nfsrvd_deallocate(nd, isdgram, vp, exp) at nfs_nfsdserv.c:5872-5972 and the start of the next function, so it is fixed under the real name of the NFSv4.2 DEALLOCATE service. Precondition: nd holds the request positioned at the DEALLOCATE arguments (stateid, offset, length), vp is a locked, referenced vnode that this function takes over, exp is the export. Return paths: (1) if NFSM_DISSECT cannot obtain the arguments it goes to nfsmout, does vput(vp) and returns that error (EBADRPC); (2) otherwise it always reaches the end, does vput(vp) once and returns 0, with the outcome in nd->nd_repstat. The statuses, evaluated in this order while nd_repstat is still 0: NFSERR_NOTSUPP for a DS server (set before any check), NFSERR_FBIG when off < 0 or the end offset exceeds NFSRV_MAXFILESIZE, NFSERR_INVAL when len == 0 or the end offset is below the start (a negative len is replaced by OFF_MAX), NFSERR_WRONGTYPE when vp is not a regular file, the status of nfsvno_getattr (which is called regardless, fetching the owner), the nfsvno_accchk(VWRITE) result when the file owner differs from the caller or the export has strict access checking, the nfsrv_lockctrl result when the stateid is not the all-ones/0x55555555 proxy stateid, and finally the status of nfsvno_deallocate. If nd_repstat is 0 at the end the deallocation was applied by nfsvno_deallocate; the function itself builds no reply data.
note: Slice 5945-6207 is the tail of nfsrvd_deallocate (:5872) plus the start of nfsrvd_copy_file_range; fixed under real name instead of dropping (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose omitted NFSERR_NOTSUPP/FBIG/INVAL and said the function returns the mbuf parse error 'when it completes' wrongly worded; checked against :5886-5971.

name: nfsrvd_compound
prose: Static function nfsrvd_compound(nd, isdgram, tag, taglen, minorvers) at nfs_nfsdsocket.c:708-1444 (the slice cut the head). It returns void; its results are the reply built in nd and nd->nd_repstat. Entry: nd holds a dissected NFSv4 COMPOUND request; taglen < 0 means that parsing the tag/minor version failed earlier. The function first takes either the V4 root lock (nfsv4_lock, then it may update the stable-storage file and expire clients and releases the lock with a reference count) or only a reference count (nfsv4_getref), and in every case releases that reference (nfsv4_relref) at the exit label nfsmout. Flow: if taglen < 0 it sets error to EBADRPC and jumps to nfsmout before the tag is copied, so no tag is written in that case; otherwise it copies the tag into the reply and reserves the result-count word, reads the operation count, sets nd_repstat to NFSERR_MINORVERMISMATCH (and runs zero operations) for an unsupported or out-of-range minor version, then loops over the operations. For each it writes the opcode and either a status word or, on success, 0; the status is nfsd_errmap(nd) for a nonzero nd_repstat, and the loop stops after the first operation that leaves nd_repstat nonzero. nd_repstat is set by this function to NFSERR_OPILLEGAL (opcode out of range or not valid for the negotiated minor version), NFSERR_MOVED (a referral on the current file handle for an operation other than GETATTR that allows it), NFSERR_SEQUENCEPOS, NFSERR_OPNOTINSESS or NFSERR_NOTONLYOP (NFSv4.1 sequencing rules), NFSERR_RESOURCE (only at the first operation, when the reply cache is flooded or malloc/mbuf memory is near its limit), NFSERR_NOFILEHANDLE, NFSERR_RESTOREFH, NFSERR_XDEV, NFSERR_PERM (vnode lock failure) or a status returned by file-handle conversion or the operation routine. An error value returned by an operation routine is mapped: EBADRPC or NFSERR_BADXDR becomes nd_repstat = NFSERR_BADXDR, any other value is copied into nd_repstat. A failure of NFSM_DISSECT or of file-handle parsing, or taglen < 0, reaches nfsmout with error EBADRPC, and nfsmout then sets nd_repstat = NFSERR_BADXDR (an error of any other kind there is only logged); nd_repstat is never left as EBADRPC. Only when an operation returns ERELOOKUP is there a rollback: nd_md and nd_dpos are reset to the values saved for that operation, the partial reply is trimmed with nfsm_trimtrailing, and the operation is retried (ND_ERELOOKUP set); ordinary failed operations are not rolled back, their opcode and error status remain in the reply. At nfsmout it writes the final reply word (the count of operations answered, retops, or two zero words when taglen < 0), vrele()s the current file-handle vnode and the saved-file-handle vnode if non-NULL, restores nd_cred if root credentials were substituted for a machine-credential operation (and frees the root credential), and releases the V4 root reference.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :708); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (tag not copied when taglen < 0; EBADRPC returned before nfsm_strtom) right (:842-847): tag sentence fixed. Old prose also wrong on: final nd_repstat 'EBADRPC' (code maps to NFSERR_BADXDR, :1370-1371, :1419-1420) and 'reply rolled back to saved cursors' for failing operations (only for ERELOOKUP retry, :1379-1394).

name: nfsrv_lockctrl
prose: Function nfsrv_lockctrl(vp, new_stpp, new_lopp, cfp, clientid, stateidp, exp, nd, p) at nfs_nfsdstate.c:1816-2552 (the slice cut the head and ends inside the next function, nfsrv_opencheck). Precondition: vp is a locked vnode (it is unlocked and re-locked internally only when local locking is enabled), *new_stpp describes the operation (flags NFSLCK_LOCK, UNLOCK, TEST, CHECK or SETATTR), *new_lopp is non-NULL because the lock range is read for LOCK, UNLOCK, TEST and CHECK, and for the LOCK/UNLOCK cases both structures should be malloc'd (a TEST/CHECK caller may use stack structures, since they are not consumed); the caller does not hold the NFS state lock. The function returns 0 on success or an error value; the error is the first of: the result of nfsrv_checkrestart, NFSERR_RESOURCE (LOCK and the state limit exceeded), errors found while looking up the client and stateid (nfsrv_getclient, nfsrv_getstate, NFSERR_BADSTATEID for a wrong-type or wrong-file stateid, nfsrv_checkseqid, NFSERR_BADSEQID for an existing lock owner on NFSv4.0, NFSERR_OLDSTATEID), nfsrv_checkgrace, NFSERR_NOGRACE, then nd->nd_repstat or the error from nfsrv_getlockfh/nfsrv_getlockfile/nfsrv_locallock, NFSERR_EXPIRED (no lockfile and not LockT; for CHECK/SETATTR without a special stateid NFSERR_BADSTATEID, and 0 for LockT or a special stateid), NFSERR_OPENMODE (access bits do not match the open, or a conflicting deny), NFSERR_PERM, NFSERR_DENIED, NFSERR_RECLAIMCONFLICT or NFSERR_LOCKED for a conflicting lock, errors from nfsrv_cleandeleg/nfsrv_delegconflict, and NFSERR_SERVERFAULT if the vnode is doomed after re-locking. Success effects: for UNLOCK nfsrv_updatelock removes the range and the stateid seqid is advanced (skipping 0 on NFSv4.1+); for LOCK with an existing lock owner nfsrv_updatelock adds the range and the seqid is advanced; for an open-to-lock-owner LOCK the new lock owner nfsstate is initialised, linked into the client's state hash and the open's list, the reply-cache entry is referenced (nfsrvd_refcache) and *new_lopp and *new_stpp are set to NULL; with local locking, the local locks are committed or the local unlock is done; TEST and CHECK create and change no lock or open state (they renew the client lease and may delay a delegation timeout), SETATTR calls nfsrv_cleandeleg and then returns 0 unless it was combined with CHECK and open, lock or delegation state still exists, in which case checking continues. When a conflicting lock is found and cfp is non-NULL (and nfsrv_clientconflict returned 0), cfp is filled with it. On every return the NFS state lock has been released, the V4 root lock is released if it was taken (haslock), vp is re-locked if the function unlocked it, and other_lop is freed unless it was consumed. On an error return with local locking active, local locks are rolled back and nfsrv_unlocklf is called, with one exception: when a conflicting lock is found and nfsrv_clientconflict returns 2 (NFSERR_PERM), the code at the conflict exit rolls back and unlocks only when that return was 0, so that path returns without the rollback and nfsrv_unlocklf.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :1816); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (ret == 2 / NFSERR_PERM path skips local-lock rollback and nfsrv_unlocklf) right (:2449-2470, rollback conditional on ret == 0): prose qualified. Old prose also wrong: 'takes a reference on its open owner' (code calls nfsrvd_refcache on the reply-cache entry, :2507), 'a test/check changes no state' (lease renewal, delegation timeout), 'on error any local locks are rolled back' without the exception.

name: nfsrv_openctrl
prose: The slice is the middle of nfsrv_openctrl(nd, vp, new_stpp, clientid, stateidp, delegstateidp, rflagsp, exp, p, filerev) at nfs_nfsdstate.c:2813-3452 (there is no function nfsrv_open in this file), so it is fixed under its real name. Precondition: *new_stpp is a malloc'd nfsstate describing the open request (access/deny bits, claim flags, owner), vp is the file's vnode, and the caller holds no NFS state lock. The function allocates a nfslockfile, an open nfsstate and a delegation nfsstate (and a scratch buffer) up front. Return value: 0 or an error. Error returns: NFSERR_EXPIRED if nfsrv_checkrestart fails, if nfsrv_getclient fails, if a claim-delegate-current has no matching current delegation or asks for write access on a read delegation, or if a claim-delegate-previous finds no old delegation; the error of nfsrv_getlockfh or nfsrv_getlockfile; NFSERR_PERM, NFSERR_RECLAIMCONFLICT or NFSERR_SHAREDENIED when nfsrv_clientconflict reports a share conflict (return 2, reclaim, or otherwise); the error of nfsrv_delegconflict when it fails other than with a retry (-1 restarts at tryagain); and NFSERR_RECLAIMCONFLICT when a delegation reclaim finds an existing delegation or open for the client and owner. When it returns 0 it has either created a new open for the file (new owner, or existing owner with no open for this file, or by upgrading the open of the same owner and file with the new share bits), or converted an unconfirmed owner's open to the new request (setting NFSV4OPEN_RESULTCONFIRM in *rflagsp), or, for claim-previous with a delegation, created the delegation plus an associated open (or moved an old delegation to the current list), and it copies the open's stateid into *stateidp; delegation issuance goes through nfsrv_issuedelegation and sets delegation bits in *rflagsp and the stateid in *delegstateidp. A new open owner consumes *new_stpp, which is then set to NULL; the NFSv4.1+ first-open case also writes a stable-storage timestamp after the locks are released. On every return the NFS state lock and (if it was taken, haslock) the V4 root lock are released, and the unused preallocated nfslockfile, open and delegation structures and the scratch buffer are freed; on the early restart-check failure only the scratch buffer pointer (NULL at that point) is freed.
note: Slice 3150-3438 is the middle of nfsrv_openctrl (:2813); fixed under the real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said 'preallocated new_open/new_deleg/new_stp held by caller' (only *new_stpp comes from the caller) and 'on failure preallocated entries freed' (only the new_open/new_deleg/new_lfp allocated here, not new_stp). Claims in the new prose checked against :2829-3451; the per-case state building (:3117-3421) is summarised, not enumerated.

name: nfsrv_checkreclaimcomplete
prose: Function nfsrv_checkreclaimcomplete(nd, onefs) at nfs_nfsdstate.c:6146-6175 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). Precondition: nd->nd_sessionid identifies the session to look up (it need not exist) and onefs is any int; the caller holds neither the NFS state lock nor a session-hash lock. The function takes the NFS state lock and the session-hash lock for nd_sessionid and then looks up the session with nfsrv_findsession. Return paths: (1) no session matches: both locks are released and NFSERR_BADSESSION is returned, with no client state changed; (2) onefs is nonzero: LCL_RECLAIMONEFS is set in the session's client flags and 0 is returned (LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE is not examined); (3) onefs is zero and LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE is already set: NFSERR_COMPLETEALREADY is returned with no change; (4) onefs is zero and LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE is not set: it sets LCL_RECLAIMCOMPLETE, calls nfsrv_markreclaim on the client and returns 0. In paths (2)-(4) both locks are released before returning (path (1) releases them before its own return), so the caller holds no lock afterwards.

name: smbfs_writevnode
prose: Function smbfs_writevnode(vp, uiop, cred, ioflag) at smbfs_io.c:249-309 (the slice starts after its head and also contains smbfs_doio and following code; the real name is smbfs_writevnode, not smbfs_write). name: tarfs_strtofflags
prose: Function tarfs_strtofflags(str, end) at tarfs_subr.c:502-537 (the slice cut the head; there is no function named tarfs_parse_flags). Precondition: str points to a NUL-terminated string and end is a non-NULL pointer to a char * (the function reads *end at its exit, so end itself must not be NULL; the pointed-to value may be NULL). It walks str as comma-separated tokens; a token is scanned character by character and parsing stops (jump to the exit) at the first character that is not between 'a' and 'z' and is not a comma or NUL; otherwise the token is compared for exact equality against each name in the static tarfs_flags table (nodump, uchg, uappnd, opaque, uunlnk, arch, schg, sappnd, sunlnk) and, on the first exact match, its flag is OR'd into the result; if no table entry matches (this includes an empty token, e.g. a leading comma, doubled comma or trailing comma, because no table name is empty), parsing stops. Return value: the OR of the flags of the tokens fully matched before parsing stopped (0 if none or if str is empty); a token that caused the stop contributes nothing. At the exit, if *end is non-NULL on entry, it is set to the position in str where parsing stopped: the offending character of an invalid token, or the end of an unmatched token (the comma that follows it, or the terminating NUL if it was last), or the terminating NUL when the whole string was consumed; if *end is NULL on entry it is left unchanged. The result is a pointer into str, no memory is allocated or freed, and only debug logging has other effects.

name: tarfs_alloc_one
prose: The slice is the middle of the static function tarfs_alloc_one(tmp, blknump) at tarfs_vfsops.c:432-845 (there is no function tarfs_parse_header), so it is fixed under its real name. Precondition: tmp is an initialized tarfs mount whose backing tar file can be read, and *blknump is the block number of the next tar header to read. It reads one 512-byte header (looping back to 'again' after an extended header or a first zero block), and returns 0 on success or when the archive ends, otherwise a positive errno. Return paths: (1) a read error from tarfs_io_read_buf is returned as that errno, and a short read (fewer than 512 bytes for a header, or fewer than the extended-header size) gives EIO; (2) two consecutive all-zero blocks: tmp->nblocks is set, *blknump is set to TAR_EOF and 0 is returned (an extended header still held is freed); (3) header magic: a GNU tar header gives EFTYPE, any other non-ustar header gives EINVAL; a bad checksum gives EINVAL; an unparsable size or modification time gives EINVAL (an invalid mode becomes S_IRUSR, and an invalid uid or gid is replaced by the root's and clears the setuid or setgid bit, neither being an error); (4) a global extended header (typeflag 'g') is skipped by advancing past its data; a second extended header before a file header gives EFTYPE, and a malformed extended-header record (bad length, no '=' or a bad numeric value for size, GNU.sparse.* or SCHILY.fflags) or one that overruns the data gives EINVAL; (5) after the extended-header data is merged (path, linkpath, size, sparse fields, flags), an inconsistent sparse description gives EINVAL; the name comes from the extended header, or prefix/name from the header; tarfs_lookup_path failure gives EINVAL; a path that already exists is skipped (success) if the new entry is a directory, and gives EINVAL otherwise; (6) by typeflag it calls tarfs_alloc_node for a directory, regular file (plus tarfs_load_blockmap if sparse), hard link (EINVAL if the target is missing, not a regular file, or itself a link, and increments the target's link count), symbolic link (EINVAL if the target is empty), block or character device (EINVAL for an invalid major or minor), and EINVAL for any other typeflag, returning an error from tarfs_alloc_node or tarfs_load_blockmap unchanged; (7) on success it advances blknum by the data size in blocks, stores it in tmp->nblocks and *blknump, and returns 0. On every return other than the TAR_EOF return in (2), exthdr and the name buffer are freed; *blknump is not updated on errors, and a node created earlier in the call is not freed here.
note: Slice is inside tarfs_alloc_one (:433); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). The old prose said 'error EINVAL/EFTYPE and control jumps to cleanup, success allocates a node or skips' only; this version lists the paths (:456-845). Hand-checked that the GNU-tar branch tests magic twice (:489-490) but that does not change which errors are returned.

name: tarfs_readdir
prose: Static VOP_READDIR method tarfs_readdir(ap) at tarfs_vnops.c:307-508 (the slice starts before it and ends before its final return). Precondition: ap->a_vp is a tarfs vnode and ap->a_uio is a valid uio; when the '..' entry will be produced, the directory's tarfs_node has a non-NULL parent (MPASS); every child's name must fit in the dirent d_name field, but the only length assertion made is MPASS(tnp->namelen < sizeof(cde.d_name)) on the directory's own name, so the child names are not checked before the memcpy. Return paths: (1) ENOTDIR if a_vp is not a directory; (2) uio_offset == TARFS_COOKIE_EOF: sets *a_eofflag to 1 if non-NULL and returns 0 with uio_offset unchanged and no cookies; (3) a uiomove failure while writing '.' or '..' is returned at once, before the common exit (uio_offset, the saved resume state and *a_eofflag are not updated by that exit); (4) otherwise it writes '.' (when uio_offset is TARFS_COOKIE_DOT), then '..' (when uio_offset is TARFS_COOKIE_DOTDOT, including right after '.'), then the children in list order, taking the start child from the first child or, when resuming, from tarfs_lookup_dir for uio_offset (EINVAL if that lookup fails), and leaves through the common exit ('done'): a uiomove failure on a child gives that error; a child of unexpected vnode type panics; an entry that does not fit in uio_resid ends the loop with EINVAL if no entry has yet been written by this call (the count includes '.' and '..') and 0 otherwise. At the common exit, if no child is pending (the list is exhausted, the directory has no children, the failure was on the lookup, or the stop happened before any child was selected, which includes when '.' or '..' did not fit, so children may remain) it sets uio_offset to TARFS_COOKIE_EOF and the directory's lastcookie to 0 and lastnode to NULL; otherwise it saves the pending child's inode number and node as lastcookie/lastnode (uio_offset already holds that inode number). It sets *a_eofflag, if non-NULL, to 1 exactly when the error is 0 and no child is pending, and to 0 otherwise. When the error is 0 and both a_cookies and a_ncookies are non-NULL it allocates (M_WAITOK, M_TEMP) an array of ndirents off_t cookies, stores it in *a_cookies and the count in *a_ncookies, filling it with the successive resume offsets; the caller must free it, and the code asserts (MPASS) that the last cookie equals the final uio_offset. In the case of an empty directory where '..' was written, that entry is not counted in ndirents (the count is skipped when the first child is NULL).
note: tarfs_vnops.c:307-508. Reviewer o1 (EOF set and uio_offset EOF when '..' does not fit although list not exhausted; EINVAL omitted) right (:380-381, :453-469). Reviewer r2 (0/eofflag=1 also when '..' written and no children) right (:387-389, :462-465). Reviewer r15 (assertion is on tnp->namelen, the directory's name, not the child's) right (:434): precondition corrected. New observation: empty-directory case does not count '..' in ndirents (:388-393).

name: tmpfs_chtimes
prose: Function tmpfs_chtimes(vp, vap, cred, td) at tmpfs_subr.c:2286-2321 (the slice cut the head and also contains tmpfs_itimes and tmpfs_truncate). Precondition: vp is an exclusively locked vnode of a tmpfs mount (ASSERT_VOP_ELOCKED at entry and exit), vap points to an initialized vattr whose va_atime, va_mtime and va_birthtime tv_sec may be VNOVAL, and cred and td identify the caller. Return paths: (1) EROFS if the mount has MNT_RDONLY, with nothing modified; (2) EPERM if tn_flags has IMMUTABLE or APPEND, with nothing modified; (3) the nonzero error of vn_utimes_perm, with nothing modified; (4) otherwise 0, after: setting tn_accessed to true if va_atime.tv_sec is not VNOVAL; setting TMPFS_NODE_MODIFIED in tn_status if va_mtime.tv_sec or va_birthtime.tv_sec is not VNOVAL; calling tmpfs_itimes(vp, &va_atime, &va_mtime), which returns at once if tn_accessed is false and neither MODIFIED nor CHANGED is set, and otherwise, under the node lock, copies the given atime into tn_atime if tn_accessed is set, copies the given mtime into tn_mtime if MODIFIED is set (copying va_mtime as given, even when its tv_sec is VNOVAL, for instance when only the birth time was requested), sets tn_ctime to the current time if CHANGED is set, and clears MODIFIED, CHANGED and tn_accessed; and finally storing va_birthtime into tn_birthtime if its tv_sec is not VNOVAL. vp stays locked and the function acquires and releases no references or memory.
