name: tmpfs_rename
prose: Static VOP_RENAME method tmpfs_rename(v) at tmpfs_vnops.c:1048-1367 (the slice cut the head). Entry state assumed by the code: fdvp and fvp are referenced and not locked, tdvp and, if non-NULL, tvp are locked and referenced (they are released with vput at the end). The function takes the source directory lock itself when fdvp differs from both tdvp and tvp. Flags accepted are AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE and AT_RENAME_EXCHANGE; other flag bits give EOPNOTSUPP. Exit paths: (1) label out, reached for EXDEV (source or target on another mount), EOPNOTSUPP, and fvp == tvp (error 0, nothing renamed); (2) when fdvp must be locked and vn_lock(LK_NOWAIT) fails, tmpfs_rename_relock is called, and if it fails its error is returned directly from this function without the releases below; after a successful relock it returns EEXIST (if AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE was given and tvp exists, checked only in this relock path of this function) or 0 (if fvp == tvp) through out_locked; (3) label out_locked, which unlocks fdvp if this function locked it (fdvp differs from tdvp and tvp) and falls into out; used by EINVAL (source name is '.' or ISDOTDOT), ENOENT (source entry not found, or the target entry not found for exchange), EPERM (tvp node with NOUNLINK/IMMUTABLE/APPEND, tdvp with APPEND/IMMUTABLE when tvp exists, the source node with NOUNLINK/IMMUTABLE/APPEND, or the source directory with APPEND/IMMUTABLE), ENOTEMPTY, ENOTDIR and EISDIR (non-exchange only: replacing a non-empty directory, with whiteout-only contents allowed under IGNOREWHITEOUT, or a directory/non-directory mismatch), the error of tmpfs_rename_check_parent when a directory moves to another parent, and the success paths. Success paths: with AT_RENAME_EXCHANGE it makes the two directory entries refer to each other's nodes (adjusting parent pointers for moved directories), purges and re-enters the name cache and updates both directories' status and times (no names change); otherwise it detaches the source entry, adds or removes whiteouts as the componentnames request, renames the entry in place if the name changed, detaches and frees any existing target entry (clearing whiteouts of a replaced directory and marking its node changed), attaches the entry to the target directory and updates the name cache. In all cases at out it ends the seqc write sections it began, releases tdvp (vrele if tdvp == tvp, else vput), vputs tvp if non-NULL, vreles fdvp and fvp, and returns error; ownership of all four references is consumed on every path except the tmpfs_rename_relock failure return in (2).
note: Slice cut head (function starts :1049); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (claims AT_RENAME_EXCHANGE swaps entries; code has no exchange path) wrong: exchange handled at :1090, :1143-1164, :1249-1268. Qualified old prose: EEXIST for AT_RENAME_NOREPLACE is only produced in the relock path (:1109-1112); the prose previously said it always applied.

name: g_journal_worker
prose: Static function g_journal_worker(arg) at g_journal.c:2012-2176 (the slice cut the head and includes the following functions up to part of g_journal_create). It is the kproc entry point for a gjournal device. Precondition: arg points to a fully set up g_journal_softc (queues, mutex sc_mtx, consumers, geom), and the thread holds neither the topology lock nor sc_mtx. Startup, executed once: it sets its priority, calls g_journal_initialize (if GJF_DEVICE_CLEAN is set) or g_journal_sync, probes BIO_FLUSH support with g_io_flush on the journal consumer and, if different, the data consumer (setting GJ_FLUSH_JOURNAL / GJ_FLUSH_DATA), then under the topology lock creates the '<name>.journal' provider with the softc's media and sector sizes and marks it available, releases the topology lock, and releases sc->sc_rootmount (root_mount_rel, then sets it to NULL) if it is non-NULL. Main loop: with sc_mtx taken it takes the first bio from the back queue, otherwise from the regular queue. If both are empty (or on a jump from the delayed-write case below) it examines the flags: with GJF_DEVICE_SWITCH or GJF_DEVICE_DESTROY set and sc_current_count > 0 it runs g_journal_flush and g_journal_flush_send and loops; with a flush or copy in progress it waits (g_journal_wait); with GJF_DEVICE_SWITCH set it runs g_journal_switch, wakes sc_journal_copying and loops; with GJF_DEVICE_DESTROY set (and SWITCH not set) it sets sc->sc_worker to NULL, wakes up &sc->sc_worker, unlocks sc_mtx and ends the kproc with kproc_exit(0), which is the only normal way out; otherwise it waits. A regular WRITE found at the head while GJF_DEVICE_SWITCH is set is not dequeued and goes to the same flag examination, so that exit can also be reached while such a write is still queued. A dequeued bio is dispatched with sc_mtx released: regular READ to g_journal_read, regular WRITE to g_journal_add_request plus g_journal_flush_send, copy READ/WRITE to the copy completion routines plus g_journal_copy_send, journal bios to g_journal_flush_done plus g_journal_flush_send; any other bio_cmd for regular or copy bios, or an unknown or GJ_BIO_READ type, panics. The function never returns to its caller.
note: Slice cut head (function starts :2013); fixed under real name. Reviewer r15 (exit only when both bio queues are empty; check sits under bp == NULL) partly right: exit check is under the try_switch label (:2090-2117), reached when both queues are empty and also by goto from a delayed WRITE during SWITCH (:2126-2130), so the exit is not strictly limited to empty queues; prose states this. Also added: exit needs DESTROY and not SWITCH (SWITCH is handled first, :2104-2109).

name: g_mirror_try_destroy
prose: Function g_mirror_try_destroy(sc) at g_mirror.c:1901-1931 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). Precondition: sc is a valid mirror softc and the caller holds sc->sc_lock exclusively. If sc->sc_rootmount is non-NULL it is released with root_mount_rel and set to NULL. The topology lock is then taken, and every path releases it again before returning. Return paths: (1) if g_mirror_can_destroy(sc) reports the device cannot be destroyed, it releases the topology lock and returns 0, with sc->sc_lock still held and the root mount already released; (2) otherwise it sets sc->sc_geom->softc and sc->sc_sync.ds_geom->softc to NULL, releases the topology lock and returns 1, after one of: if G_MIRROR_DEVICE_FLAG_DRAIN is set, it releases sc->sc_lock with sx_xunlock, calls wakeup(&sc->sc_worker) (the wait channel address; no specific thread handle) and then sets sc->sc_worker to NULL (this store happens after sc_lock was dropped), so sc_lock is no longer held on return; if the DRAIN flag is not set, it calls g_mirror_destroy_device(sc) with sc_lock still held at the call, and the softc is not accessed by this function afterwards.
note: g_mirror.c:1901-1931. Reviewer o1 (DRAIN path unconditionally unlocks sc_lock) right (:1923) and r2 (wakeup is on &sc->sc_worker and sets sc_worker to NULL, not a worker thread) right (:1924-1925); both already in the old prose, which was re-checked and kept with two added details (sc_worker store after unlock, root mount released before can_destroy test).

name: g_mirror_config
prose: The slice is the tail of g_mirror_config(req, mp, verb) at g_mirror_ctl.c:1088-1129, the gctl verb dispatcher of the mirror class, so it is fixed under that name instead of being dropped. It returns void. Precondition: the topology lock is held on entry (g_topology_assert), req is a gctl request and verb is a NUL-terminated string. Behaviour: if the 'version' parameter is absent it calls gctl_error ('No version argument') and returns with the topology lock still held; if the version differs from G_MIRROR_VERSION it calls gctl_error ('out of sync') and returns, again with the topology lock held; otherwise it releases the topology lock, then calls exactly one handler chosen by string comparison of verb: configure, create, rebuild, insert, remove, resize, deactivate, forget, stop (g_mirror_ctl_stop with 0), destroy (g_mirror_ctl_stop with 1), or, for any other verb, gctl_error ('Unknown verb.'). It then takes the topology lock again before returning. Errors from the handlers are reported through the gctl request, not through a return value.
note: Slice 1105-1129 is the end of g_mirror_config (:1089); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose omitted the two early returns (version missing or mismatched) in which the topology lock is not released (:1095-1103).

name: g_part_bsd_write
prose: Function g_part_bsd_write(basetable, cp) at g_part_bsd.c:497-539 (the slice cut the head). Precondition: basetable is a BSD partition table whose bbarea buffer has room for the label (at least BBSIZE bytes) and for gpt_entries 16-byte slots at offset sectorsize + 148, whose entry list holds entries in ascending gpe_index order, and cp is a consumer opened for writing whose provider has a valid sectorsize. For each slot number index from 1 to gpt_entries the function looks at the entry pointer it holds (initially the first list entry): if that entry's gpe_index equals index, the slot at bbarea + sectorsize + 148 + (index - 1) * 16 is filled from the entry's partition data (size, offset, fsize, fstype, frag, cpg) when the entry is not marked deleted, and zeroed when it is marked deleted; if no list entry matches index, the slot is zeroed; the entry pointer advances to the next list entry whenever one matched (deleted or not). Entries with a gpe_index above gpt_entries, or out of ascending order, are not written. It then zeroes the 16-bit checksum field at label + 136, stores in it the XOR of the little-endian 16-bit words from the start of the label up to (not including) label + 148 + gpt_entries * 16, and writes BBSIZE bytes of bbarea at offset 0 of the provider with g_write_data. It returns the error from g_write_data (0 on success); the label updates remain in bbarea whether or not the write succeeds. No locks or references are taken or released.
note: g_part_bsd_write is at :497 (slice cut head). Reviewer r15 (matching but deleted entry's slot is zeroed, not only the no-entry case) right (:515-523): added. Also added that only in-order entries are matched (:513, :525-526).

name: g_part_gpt_setunset
prose: Function g_part_gpt_setunset(basetable, baseentry, attrib, set) at g_part_gpt.c:1110-1193 (the slice also contains neighbouring functions). The attribute name attrib is compared case-insensitively; baseentry may be NULL. Return paths in code order: (1) attrib 'active' under Boot Camp (table->bootcamp): ENXIO if the entry is NULL, EINVAL if baseentry->gpe_index is greater than NDOSPART, otherwise it sets byte 0 of each of the NDOSPART MBR partition slots, slot gpe_index - 1 getting 0x80 when set is nonzero and 0 when it is zero, and all other slots getting 0, and returns 0; (2) 'active' without Boot Camp: ENXIO if the entry is non-NULL, otherwise it sets byte 0 of each MBR slot whose type byte is 0xee to 0x80 (set nonzero) or 0 (set zero) and byte 0 of every other slot to 0, and returns 0; (3) 'lenovofix': ENXIO if the entry is non-NULL, otherwise it zeroes the MBR partition table, writes a 0xee protective entry (start 1, size limited to UINT32_MAX) into MBR slot index 1 when set is nonzero and slot index 0 when set is zero, and returns 0 (it reads the first consumer's provider of the geom for the media size, so a consumer must exist); (4) for any other attrib, ENODEV if the entry is NULL, whatever the name; (5) with a non-NULL entry, EINVAL if attrib is not 'bootme', 'bootonce' or 'bootfailed'; (6) otherwise the corresponding attribute bit (BOOTME, BOOTONCE or BOOTFAILED, plus the BOOTME bit when 'bootonce' is set, but not cleared when 'bootonce' is cleared) is ORed into ent_attr when set is nonzero or cleared when it is zero; if the resulting value differs from the old one it is stored and, when the entry was not newly created (gpe_created is clear), baseentry->gpe_modified is set to 1; it returns 0 also when nothing changed. The function allocates nothing and takes no lock or reference.
note: g_part_gpt.c:1111-1193. Reviewer o1 (active/lenovofix success updates the MBR, not ent_attr or gpe_modified) right (:1124-1161), r2 (lenovofix writes the 0xee entry into slot index 0 when unset, bootonce set also sets BOOTME) right and already stated. New: an unknown attribute with a NULL entry returns ENODEV, not EINVAL (:1163-1164, :1180-1181); old prose said EINVAL for any unrecognised name.

name: ddf_meta_read
prose: Function ddf_meta_read(cp, meta) at md_ddf.c:1048-1284 (the slice cut the head and runs into ddf_meta_write). Precondition: cp is a geom consumer whose provider has a sectorsize and mediasize, and meta is a ddf_meta whose previous contents may be discarded (it is freed with ddf_meta_free at entry). Return paths: (1) ENXIO if the provider sectorsize is smaller than a struct ddf_header; (2) the g_read_data error if the anchor block (the last sector) cannot be read; (3) EINVAL if the anchor has neither big- nor little-endian DDF signature, is not of header type anchor, has a CRC mismatch, or has a primary header LBA or (when it is not -1) secondary header LBA that lies too close to or beyond the end of the media; (4) otherwise it reads the primary header (lba = plba) and then, one after another, the controller data, physical-disk, virtual-disk, configuration, physical-disk-data and, when the header records one, bad-block-management sections; for the primary copy, any failure after the anchor checks, whether a read error or a header check failure (signature or CRC or GUID differing from the anchor, LBA fields differing from the anchor, wrong header type, section extents beyond the media, a section length of maxphys or more, a bad signature on the controller, physical-disk, virtual-disk, physical-disk-data or BBM section, or no matching physical-disk record for the pdd reference), causes the whole read to restart, with meta freed, from the secondary header if one is recorded (slba != -1); (5) if that retry, or the only copy, fails on a read the g_read_data error is returned, and if it fails a check EINVAL is returned; (6) on success it returns 0 with meta->sectorsize and meta->bigendian set and meta->hdr (a copy of the primary or secondary header, whose CRC field was overwritten with 0xffffffff), cdr, pdr, vdr, cr, pdd and, if a BBM log was present, bbm holding malloc'd copies of the on-disk records, which the caller releases with ddf_meta_free. On every nonzero return meta has been freed and holds no buffers; the anchor buffer is freed on all paths after it was read. The configuration records have no signature check.

name: g_raid_md_ctl_ddf
prose: The slice is the middle of g_raid_md_ctl_ddf(md, req) at md_ddf.c:2257-2732, the gctl command handler of the DDF metadata module, so it is fixed under that name instead of being dropped. Precondition: md is the DDF metadata object, req carries the 'verb' string and an 'nargs' integer (both are dereferenced without a NULL check) and the thread does not hold the topology lock (it takes and releases it itself around consumer opening). It returns 0 on success or a negative code, and all negative codes except -100 are accompanied by gctl_error. Verbs: (1) 'label': -1 if nargs < 4, -2 no volume name, -3 no RAID level, -4 unknown level, -5 unsupported level or disk count; then for each disk argument ('NONE' skipped) -6 missing disk name, -7 if an existing disk is not active or has no free partition, -8 if the disk cannot be opened (a loop error destroys the disk objects created in this call that are still in state NONE, then returns); afterwards -8 if no sector size was obtained, -9 size larger than the available space, -10 strip smaller than the sector size, -11 strip not a multiple of the sector size, -13 size too small after rounding (these later returns do not destroy the disk objects created for the call); on success it creates the volume, its metadata and subdisks, activates the disks and subdisks, writes the metadata, refills from spare disks, sends the start event and returns 0. (2) 'add': always -99 (not applicable). (3) 'delete': with a single argument equal to the node name it returns -4 if force is supplied as 0 and some volume is open, otherwise erases metadata on every disk, destroys the node and returns 0; with more than two arguments -1; -2 if no volume name, -3 if the volume (found by name, provider name, 'raid/' name or numeric global id) is not found, -4 if force is supplied as 0 and the volume is open; otherwise, if there are at least two volumes it destroys the volume, purges disks and writes metadata, and if it was the last volume it erases metadata on all disks and destroys the node, and returns 0. (4) 'remove' and 'fail': -1 if nargs < 2; for each disk argument -2 for a missing name and -3 for a disk not found, either of which stops the loop; 'fail' marks the disk failed, 'remove' erases its metadata and destroys it; after the loop (also after an early stop, so earlier arguments stay applied) it purges volumes and writes metadata, destroys the node if no disks remain, else refills, and returns 0 or the loop's -2/-3. (5) 'insert': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk -3 missing name or -4 cannot open (stop); otherwise it makes the disk a spare, creates its metadata, writes the metadata and refills, returning 0 or the loop's error. (6) any other verb: -100 without gctl_error.
note: Slice 2388-2648 is the middle of g_raid_md_ctl_ddf (:2258); fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said '0 or a small negative code' only; new prose lists the codes per verb from :2286-2731.

name: g_raid_md_ctl_jmicron
prose: Function g_raid_md_ctl_jmicron(md, req) at md_jmicron.c:1018-1382, the gctl command handler of the JMicron metadata module (the packet name g_raid_md_jmicron_ctl_start does not exist; the slice is the middle of this function), so it is fixed instead of dropped. Precondition: req carries 'verb' and 'nargs' (both dereferenced without a NULL check) and the thread does not hold the topology lock (it takes it around consumer opening). It returns 0 or a negative code, and every negative code is accompanied by gctl_error. Verbs: (1) 'label': -1 if nargs < 4, -2 no volume name, -3 no level, -4 unknown level ('RAID5' is read as 'RAID5-LA'), -5 unsupported level or disk count; for each disk argument ('NONE' creates a placeholder disk with no consumer) -6 missing name, -7 disk cannot be opened (any disk objects created earlier in the call are not destroyed on this return); afterwards -8 if no sector size, -9 size larger than the smallest disk minus one sector, -10 strip smaller than the sector size, -11 strip not a multiple of the sector size, -12 if the strip value at that point (still the default 131072 when this check runs, since the user value is stored afterwards) is above 65535 sectors, -13 size too small after rounding, -14 size above 0xffffffffffff sectors; otherwise it creates the volume (level, strip and size computed), attaches subdisks to the created disks (active, or offline for placeholders), writes the metadata, refills from spare disks, sends the volume start event and returns 0. (2) 'delete': -4 if the force argument is present as 0 and a volume is open; otherwise it erases the metadata of every disk with a consumer, destroys the node and returns 0. (3) 'remove' and 'fail': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk argument -2 for a missing name and -3 for a disk not found, either stopping the loop; 'fail' marks the disk failed; 'remove' erases its metadata and then, if the disk was assigned a position, makes it offline, kills its consumer and disconnects its subdisks, otherwise destroys the disk; after the loop (also after an early stop) it writes the metadata and destroys the node if only offline placeholders remain, else refills; returns 0 or the loop's -2/-3. (4) 'insert': -1 if nargs < 2; per disk -3 missing name, -4 cannot open, -8 if after starting the disk it is neither active nor spare (the disk is destroyed and the loop stops); it writes the metadata if anything changed and returns 0 or the loop's error. (5) any other verb: gctl_error 'Command is not supported' and -100.

name: allocate_chunk
prose: Static function allocate_chunk(sc, comp, comp_no_p, chunk) at g_virstor.c:1801-1844 (the slice cut the head and also contains dump_component, bioq_dismantle and other code, which are not part of this function). Precondition: sc->curr_component is less than sc->n_components (KASSERTed) and comp, comp_no_p and chunk are writable. *comp is always set to the component currently selected by sc->curr_component. Return paths: (1) that component still has free chunks (chunk_next < chunk_count): *comp_no_p is set to its index, *chunk to its chunk_next (relative to the component), chunk_next is incremented, and 0 is returned; (2) the current component is full and it is the last component: an error is logged, -1 is returned, *comp still points to that full component and *comp_no_p and *chunk are not written; (3) the current component is full and a later one exists: the CURRENT flag is cleared on the old one, sc->curr_component is advanced by one, *comp points to the new component (a warning is logged when the number of remaining components is within the watermark), the new component's chunk_next is raised to its chunk_reserved if it is lower, its flags get VIRSTOR_PROVIDER_ALLOCATED and VIRSTOR_PROVIDER_CURRENT, *comp_no_p is set to the new index, *chunk to the new chunk_next, chunk_next is incremented, and 0 is returned; the code does not check that the new component itself has a free chunk. No locks are taken or released by the function.
note: Slice 1807-1904 is the body of allocate_chunk (:1802-1844) plus other functions; fixed under real name instead of dropped (HAND_METHOD rule 6). Old prose said '*comp points at the current component' and 'returns -1 when all components exhausted': *comp is advanced when switching, and -1 is returned only when the current, last, component is full (:1813-1819).
